I am specifically looking for an exchange in East Asia (Taiwan, Hong Kong, or Singapore). 
                    I want a top-tier technical university with a massive campus and high-tech labs.
                    
                    Environment: Ultra-modern, safe, and efficient cities. 
                    Focus: Semiconductor industry or Hardware/Software integration. 
                    Budget: $11,000 for the semester.

analysis.general_fit_reasoning: Low academic match for top-tier tech (business/management focus); small/semi-closed campus in a mid-sized Alpine city (pleasant outdoors but not ultra-modern megacity); modest social scene; Western Europe costs reasonable versus budget; no strong semiconductor/hardware research footprint.

academic.academic_summary_notes: Exchange students must enroll in at least 2 courses (4 credits) per semester; undergraduates can take up to 25 credits and graduates up to 20 credits. Some departments and many specific courses (e.g., practicum, certain professional programs, International College, D-School, etc.) are restricted, and students should plan preliminarily and adjust when the official course list is released.

housing_and_logistics.housing_details: Students can apply for on-campus housing during the exchange application period but accommodation is not guaranteed due to limited dormitory rooms; see https://isss.ntu.edu.tw/ >> Campus Life >> Accommodation for on- and off-campus information.
housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: Students must purchase insurance before traveling and provide proof valid for the entire exchange period: accident insurance minimum TWD 1,000,000 and medical insurance minimum TWD 1,000,000.
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: Students are responsible for applying for the proper visa via a Taiwan diplomatic mission; insurance covering accident and medical risks (minimum TWD 1,000,000 each) must be purchased prior to travel and cover the full exchange period. On-campus housing is available but limited and not guaranteed.

student_integration.integration_summary_notes: All exchange students must attend mandatory orientation activities. Each exchange student will be assigned a student volunteer for help and advice, and support for students with disabilities is available if notified during nomination.

requirements.name: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

academic.instruction_languages: English; some Humanities and Social Science courses may require Chinese (noted in course descriptions as [C], [Ca] or [Pu])
academic.academic_summary_notes: Most courses carry 3 credits (3 instructional hours/week over 13 weeks). Recommended credit load is 15 credits per term; exchange students are excluded from self‑financed programs and certain PG business courses, and PG course enrollment is generally limited to specified engineering departments.

housing_and_logistics.housing_details: Exchange students are arranged to live in university housing as space permits, typically in shared rooms. Details: http://shrl.ust.hk.
housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: Exchange students have access to on‑campus medical clinic (outpatient) and student dental clinic (charges at https://hseo.hkust.edu.hk/clinic). All exchange students are required to take out HKUST Compulsory Travel Insurance unless prior arrangement is made between HKUST and the home institution.
housing_and_logistics.estimated_housing_cost_per_month: HK$45,000 per term (includes student housing, visa and insurance; subject to increase 5-10%)
housing_and_logistics.estimated_living_cost_per_month: HK$45,000 per term (approx. US$5,800) for one term including student housing, visa and insurance; subject to increase 5-10%.
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: Overseas exchange students must obtain a student visa unless they have right of abode; HKUST sends a visa application form and processes the application on the student's behalf. Compulsory travel insurance is required for exchange students.

student_integration.integration_summary_notes: Exchange students have access to all on‑campus educational, sports and recreational facilities and student health services; specific buddy or mandatory orientation programs are not mentioned in the provided factsheet.

requirements.name: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

academic.academic_summary_notes: Undergraduate inbound exchange students must take at least 9 credits per semester (graduate students: at least 2 courses). Students may choose courses across colleges and campuses, but instructors can refuse enrollment due to prerequisites or limited capacity; some programs (e.g., College of Management) restrict eligibility to final-year undergraduates and graduate students. Course lists are finalized about two months before semester start.

housing_and_logistics.housing_details: The Division of Overseas Student Affairs provides accommodation services and host-family arrangements; no explicit deadlines, guarantees, or booking platform details are provided in the factsheet.
housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: The Division of Overseas Student Affairs assists with insurance arrangements, but no specifics on accepted coverage or costs are provided.
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: NYCU's Division of Overseas Student Affairs assists incoming students with visa, registration, accommodation, and insurance arrangements; no processing timelines or mandatory insurance details are specified in the factsheet.

student_integration.language_course_details: Free Chinese courses are offered (Chinese Cultural Salon; courses range from introductory to advanced across 4 levels; elective situational conversation courses) via the Chinese Language Division, Language Teaching and Research Center.
student_integration.integration_summary_notes: The Division of Overseas Student Affairs runs integration supports such as host-family arrangements and an international student society; free Chinese language and cultural courses are provided to help integration, though no explicit mandatory orientation or detailed buddy program description is given.

analysis.general_fit_reasoning: Solid engineering school with decent ARWU-related presence; good urban campus integrated into Montreal nightlife; costs in Canada are moderate-high for the semester; some hardware research but outside East Asia and not in the targeted semiconductor cluster.

academic.grading_system_summary: Undergraduates: DISTINCTION / PASS / FAILURE (credits awarded for DISTINCTION and PASS). Graduates: PASS / FAILURE (credits awarded for PASS).
academic.academic_summary_notes: Exchange students may take undergraduate and graduate courses in Chinese or English; some programs (Special Programs in English, Academy of Arts and Design, physical training courses and some other programs) are restricted. Cross-faculty modules are allowed but no more than 8 credits outside the student's major. Graduate students may conduct research/thesis with prior approval from a tutor. Students taking courses in English must be fluent in English.

housing_and_logistics.housing_details: On-campus accommodation prioritized at Zijing Foreign Student Apartment; newest on-campus dorm info and application instructions provided in the Welcome Package. Deposit is charged (refundable upon check-out). On-campus accommodation availability may be limited over semester breaks (on-campus housing mainly available for students with one-academic-year stays and successful reservation). Private accommodation nearby is available via agencies.
housing_and_logistics.medical_and_insurance_details: All exchange students are required to buy local student insurance (covers local accidents and urgent medications). The local insurance normally costs 400 RMB per semester.
housing_and_logistics.estimated_housing_cost_per_month: On-campus (Zijing Foreign Student Apartment, historical/typical rates): double room ~40 RMB/day (~1,200 RMB/month), single room ~80 RMB/day (~2,400 RMB/month) (quotation referenced from 2013). Private accommodation: ~1,000–2,000 RMB/month for a single room up to several thousand RMB for a full apartment. Deposit required (refundable).
housing_and_logistics.estimated_living_cost_per_month: Food/meals on campus: 50–70 RMB/day (~1,500–2,100 RMB/month). Personal expenses (laundry, sundries, local transport): 1,500–2,000 RMB/month. Academic expenses (books): 600–800 RMB/month. Note: insurance ~400 RMB/semester.
housing_and_logistics.logistics_summary_notes: Students require X1 (stays >6 months) or X2 (stays <6 months) visa; the Academic Affairs Office includes the JW202 form in the Welcome Package to assist visa applications. No airport pick-up; recommended arrival is about one week before semester start; exchange students are not allowed to work and must purchase local insurance.

student_integration.integration_summary_notes: A Buddy Program matches exchange students with a local buddy for support. Orientation is held the week before semester start and students can use most university facilities (some clubs may have constraints).
